facts: Web sync-core protocol is p2p-kanban-sync/1 and its validation does not accept a generic put operation.
Web and Android use logicalClock, replicaId, eventId ordering for deterministic conflict resolution.
Android roaming protocol is p2p-kanban-roaming/1 and encrypts event JSON with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a board capability key.
Android board.snapshot seeds a missing local snapshot and card.delete tombstones block later card.put resurrection.
A10 keeps A08 pending_local_changes separate from the durable sync_outbox protocol representation.
Fresh-host A09b UTS exposed exact getrandom 0.4.3 conflicting with secret-service 5.2.0 final offline re-resolution; A10 aligns the direct pin to getrandom 0.4.2 without weakening offline acceptance.
A10 includes a deterministic two-replica relay disruption harness that applies a dropped event after reconnect amid reorder and replay, then verifies converged card materialization.
inferences: A desktop sync core can preserve compatibility without copying PostgreSQL or Android storage by implementing the shared protocol/merge semantics behind application and repository boundaries.
Unknown/new card fields should be preserved opaquely in SQLite so a narrower native schema does not silently destroy cross-client data.
proposals: A11 should provision/import roaming capabilities and snapshots through device-link/2 without weakening the A10 merge and vault boundaries.
Relay orchestration should materialize local pending markers before pull/apply and should never treat relay acceptance as semantic application.
unresolved: Legacy roaming/1 has no post-snapshot column mutation operation; local column.create markers are blocked rather than silently lost.
Board appearance is preserved as protocol evidence but native appearance parity remains A12.
Nostr relay drop/reconnect behavior still needs the transport/coordinator layer; A10 verifies reorder/replay at the sync-core boundary only.
